fields.summary: Explains the US H-1B visa for Indian graduates, highlighting the 20,000 master's cap lottery exemption and year-round hiring at cap-exempt universities and research institutes.
Cost-saving guide for Indian students: replace $2,200 to $3,500 university health plans with qualifying ISO or PSI plans to reduce yearly medical insurance expenses.
Practical guide for Indian families documenting financial proof for Form I-20: universities require liquid savings, FDs, or loan sanction letters covering one full academic year.
Guides Indian offer holders through paying tuition seat deposits of $100 to $500 and submitting financial documents to receive their official Form I-20.
Essential checklist for Indian students landing in the US: clear CBP port of entry, retrieve your electronic Form I-94, activate mobile service, and report your local address.
Compares MS in Data Science and Business Analytics for Indian students, highlighting required STEM CIP codes that ensure 36 months of post-graduation OPT work authorization.
Highlights MEM and MIS graduate programs for Indian engineers seeking tech management careers, providing STEM work authorization without the high tuition of a traditional MBA.
Decision framework for Indian students with multiple admits: compare net costs and tech hub locations, while selecting only one SEVIS ID for your visa appointment.
Housing advice for Indian graduate students: learn how to secure off-campus apartments, find roommates, sign lease contracts, and manage security deposits near US campuses.
Explains US on-campus employment rules for Indian F-1 students, who can legally work up to 20 hours per week during semesters and 40 hours during vacations to offset living costs.
Details post-study work authorization for Indian graduates: explains how the 12-month initial OPT and 24-month STEM extension grant up to 36 months of employment with E-Verify firms.
Helps Indian non-CS engineering and science graduates transition into US computer science master's programs by completing prerequisite courses in algorithms and data structures.
Timeline strategy for Indian applicants: submitting master's applications before priority deadlines (typically mid-November to mid-December) maximizes consideration for TA and RA funding.
Compares public state flagships and private US universities for Indian families, analyzing tuition differences and explaining why top tech recruiters hire equally from public R1 schools.
Strategic advice for Indian students facing university rejections: identify application weak points, upgrade prerequisite coursework, and reapply with an improved statement of purpose.
Navigational roadmap for Indian students and families outlining the full US immigration path, from F-1 student status and CPT or OPT through to H-1B specialty worker visas.
Funding hub for Indian master's applicants, explaining the difference between university assistantship tuition waivers and external scholarships from Indian and international trusts.
Application blueprint for Indian students preparing US graduate packages: format a concise one-page resume, secure three academic LORs, and craft a compelling Statement of Purpose.
Assists Indian international students with obtaining a 9-digit Social Security Number (SSN) after securing on-campus work, enabling US credit history and tax reporting.
Directory for Indian students pursuing computer science master's programs, confirming DHS STEM designations that extend post-graduation work rights from 12 to 36 months.
